narrative: Equity markets have plunged into technical correction territory, with the S&P 500 down over 10% from record highs and the Nasdaq 100 dropping 18.4% from its October peak as the AI-driven trade rapidly unwinds following the Anthropic IPO. Market risk aversion is acute, driving the VIX above 30-35 as strong corporate earnings fail to halt selling and investors rotate into Treasuries. Macro pressure remains intense with Ed Ludlow noting the US 10-year yield posted its longest streak above 5% since 2007, raising capital costs for AI infrastructure. Tech sentiment is further battered by an SEC accounting probe into Nvidia, a short report targeting AMD, and heightened US-China export scrutiny. Meanwhile, Donald Trump criticized the Federal Reserve for politically motivated elevated rates, even as market participants increasingly debate recession risks and scale back December rate hike expectations.

Nasdaq.why: Anchors report the index is down 18.4% from its October 6 record high as AI momentum unwinds, hit by an SEC probe into Nvidia and semiconductor sector weakness.

S&P 500.why: Anchors note the index entered correction territory after sliding over 10% from record highs in its longest losing streak since 2020.

Gold.why: Anchors report gold fell between 2.65% and 4% to $3,530 per ounce amid broad-based market liquidation.

Oil.why: Anchors presented conflicting views, reporting Brent faced downward pressure at $91 in one session, while reporting modest gains for WTI and Brent in another.
